mutation.section: Preliminary Statement and Assignments of Error
mutation.description: Deleted the clause that applies the knowledge element, leaving the sentence's assertion that knowledge is not at issue standing on nothing. The negligence per se argument, the statutes and ordinances relied on, and the Shroades line of authority are unchanged.
mutation.gold_vulnerability: The brief's own statement of the rule (quoting Sikora clarifying Shroades) preserves the excuse that a landlord is not liable under R.C. 5321.04 if it neither knew nor should have known of the circumstances causing the violation. With the clause removed, nothing in the brief applies that element to this appellee, so the negligence per se argument no longer answers the defense its own rule statement invites.
mutation.why_this_is_realistic: Landlord knowledge is the element most often asserted rather than shown in habitability and lead-hazard briefing, and the control brief's own structure makes the omission invisible: the rule statement stays put in a later section, so the brief still looks like it addresses knowledge.
